title: Countable semi-free resolution over a countable DG algebra
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Assume the set $\coprod_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ is countable. For every right differential graded $A$-module $N$ whose groups $H^i(N)$ are all countable, there is a quasi-isomorphism $q:P\to N$ with the following properties. As a graded right $A$-module, $P=\bigoplus_{j\in J}x_jA$ for a countable set $J$ of homogeneous free generators. There is a function $h:J\to\mathbf N$ such that $d(x_j)$ is a finite sum $\sum_{h(k)<h(j)}x_ka_{kj}$ with homogeneous coefficients of the required degrees. The set $\coprod_iP^i$ is countable. Thus the spans of generators with $h(j)\leq r$ form an exhaustive filtration by differential graded submodules with graded-split inclusions and quotients direct sums of shifts of $A$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-countable-submodule-representative] to obtain a countable DG submodule $M\subseteq N$ whose inclusion $i$ induces all cohomology isomorphisms. It remains to construct a countable semi-free resolution of this actual DG module $M$.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), using Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, and Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve.

proof.text: Set $M_0=M$. Inductively apply [lem-sfb-dg-countable-free-cover] to the countable module $M_i$ to choose $\pi_i:Q_i\twoheadrightarrow M_i$, with basis layers $U_i,V_i$, and set $M_{i+1}=\ker\pi_i$. This is a countable DG submodule of $Q_i$, so the induction continues. Define $f_i:Q_i\to Q_{i-1}$ for $i>0$ as $\pi_i$ followed by the kernel inclusion $M_i\hookrightarrow Q_{i-1}$. Thus $f_{i-1}f_i=0$ (with $f_0=\pi_0$). The augmented chain of $Q_i$ is exact degreewise. It is exact on cocycles too: a cocycle in the kernel at $Q_i$ lies in $M_{i+1}$ and lifts to a cocycle of $Q_{i+1}$ by the cover property; cocycles of $M$ lift through $\pi_0$.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), using Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, and Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve.

proof.text: Put $P^n=\bigoplus_{i\geq0}Q_i^{n+i}$, with the unchanged right $A$-action. On $x\in Q_i^b$ put $D(x)=f_i(x)+(-1)^id_{Q_i}(x)$, interpreting the first term as zero when $i=0$. Both terms have total degree $b-i+1$. Since $f_if_{i+1}=0$ and the $f_i$ commute with the internal differentials, the two mixed terms of $D^2$ have signs $(-1)^i$ and $(-1)^{i-1}$ and cancel. For homogeneous $a$, the Leibniz coefficient is $(-1)^{i+b}=(-1)^{b-i}$, exactly the required sign in total degree $b-i$. Hence $P$ is a right DG $A$-module. Define $\epsilon:P\to M$ by $\pi_0$ on $Q_0$ and zero on $Q_i$, $i>0$; $\pi_0f_1=0$ makes this a DG map.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), using Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, and Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve.

proof.text: Forget the DG action, retaining the underlying complexes of abelian groups, regarded as $\mathbf Z$-modules. Step 2 gives precisely the exact augmented complex and exact augmented cocycle sequences required by [lem-pc-derived-total-resolution-quasi-iso]. Its column $p=-i$ is $Q_i$, so its signed direct-sum total differential is $f_i+(-1)^id_{Q_i}$ and its augmentation is $\epsilon$. Thus $H^n(\epsilon)$ is an isomorphism for every $n$. The composite $q=i\epsilon:P\to N$ is a quasi-isomorphism, since $H^n(q)=H^n(i)H^n(\epsilon)$ is a composite of isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 09IZ, lemma-good-resolution-gives-qis, applied in dga.tex Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve.

proof.text: Take $J=\coprod_{i\geq0}(U_i\amalg V_i)$, giving each basis vector its total degree $t_w-i$. Set $h(i,u)=2i$ for $u\in U_i$ and $h(i,v)=2i+1$ for $v\in V_i$. The internal differential vanishes on $e_u$ and sends $e_v$ into the span of $U_i$, with smaller height. The horizontal differential lands in $Q_{i-1}$, whose basis heights are at most $2i-1$. Every image of a basis vector has finite support, by the direct-sum definition. Consequently $D$ strictly lowers height on basis vectors. The spans of heights at most $r$ are DG submodules by Leibniz, exhaust $P$, and have graded retractions obtained by deleting other coordinates. Their quotients are direct sums of shifts of $A$, since the differential of each new basis vector is zero modulo the preceding span.

source.place: Tag 0CRM, lemma-countable, proof (2) to (1), using Tag 09KN, lemma-good-quotient, and Tag 09KP, lemma-resolve.

proof.text: Each $U_i\amalg V_i$ is countable in the sense of [def-sfb-countable-set], hence $J$, a union indexed by $\mathbf N$, is countable by [lem-trf-countable-unions]. Each homogeneous element of $P$ is a finite sum of basis vectors with homogeneous coefficients in $A$. Such sums are encoded by finite lists of elements of the countable set $J\times\coprod_kA^k$. There are countably many finite lists; adjoining the integer degree still gives a countable set. Thus $\coprod_nP^n$ is countable, as asserted.
